L17@P0: Product Description
L18@P0: Antifoams are supplied as two basic types of
L19@P0: composition or mixtures of the two. Organic antifoams
L20@P0: are of synthetic origin. Silicone-based antifoams are
L21@P0: generally considered to be siloxane polymers and are
L22@P0: also synthetic. Our suppliers generally consider the
L23@P0: exact composition to be proprietary.
L24@P0: Products A6582, A6457, A6707, A8082, and A8582 are
L25@P0: listed as Molecular Biology Grade and have been
L26@P0: tested for use in bacterial fermentation. No significant
L27@P0: inhibition is found when E. coli or B. subtilis is grown in
L28@P0: Terrific Broth supplemented with effective
L29@P0: concentrations of antifoams. These products have
L30@P0: individual data sheets available upon request.
L31@P0: Organic Antifoams
L32@P0: Antifoam 204 (A6426 and A8311)
L33@P0: Antifoam 204 contains 100% active components and is
L34@P0: a mixture of organic non-silicone polypropylene based
L35@P0: polyether dispersions. It does not contain mineral oil.
L36@P0: Antifoam 204 can itself be considered a surfactant, but
L37@P0: it contains no other surfactants. This product is
L38@P0: synthetic, and not derived from animal or plant sources.
L39@P0: Antifoam 204 can be sterilized repeatedly. The flow
L40@P0: properties of Antifoam 204 are such that it can be
L41@P0: pumped to a fermentor on an as-needed basis.
L42@P0: For use in microbiological media Sigma recommends a
L43@P0: starting concentration of between 0.005% and 0.01%.
L44@P0: The optimal amount of antifoam required for various
L45@P0: applications will need to be determined. Antifoam 204 is
L46@P0: soluble in methanol, ethanol, toluene, xylene,
L47@P0: perchloroethylene, and cold water at temperatures
L48@P0: below 15 °C. It is insoluble in warm water and ethylene
L49@P0: glycol.
L50@P0: Appearance: Clear, colorless viscous liquid
L51@P0: Density: 1.01 g/ml
L52@P0: Viscosity: 400 cps
L53@P0: Cloud Point: 18.0-21.0 °C in 1% aqueous solution
L54@P0: A8311 is supplied autoclaved for aseptic conditions.
L55@P0: Note: Antifoam 204 (100% organic defoaming agents)
L56@P0: replaces Antifoam 289 (99% organic defoamer plus 1%
L57@P0: silicon glycol as spreadability enhancer).
L58@P0: Antifoam O-30 (A8082)
L59@P0: Antifoam O-30 is completely organic, fatty acid estertype antifoam that is dispersible in water. It can be
L60@P0: repeatedly sterilized by autoclaving. The flow properties
L61@P0: of Antifoam O-30 are such that it can be pumped to a
L62@P0: fermentor on an as-needed basis.
L63@P0: Appearance: Amber-colored, clear liquid
L64@P0: Density: 0.98 g/ml
L65@P0: Silicon Antifoams
L66@P0: The active ingredient of the antifoams is a siliconebased polymer that has a molec ular weight range of
L67@P0: 3,200 to 16,500 Da. These products consist of particles
L68@P0: ranging in size from 10 to 40 microns, and can be
L69@P0: removed by filtration.
L70@P0: The silicone-type antifoams are suspensions and must
L71@P0: be agitated before a sample is taken from the container
L72@P0: to insure representative sampling. In order to remove
L73@P0: traces of these types of antifoam from glassware, wash
L74@P0: the glassware in hot soapy water followed by an alcohol
L75@P0-1: (isopropanol) wash or bleach.Autoclaving may result in phase separation and may
L76@P1: require remixing the emulsion. A different emulsifier is
L77@P1: present in each of the Antifoam emulsions.
L78@P1: Antifoam emulsions B, C, and Y-30 contain
L79@P1: preservatives to guard against microbial growth. Longterm storage of diluted material may diminish this
L80@P1: antimicrobial effect and additional preservative may be
L81@P1: required.
L82@P1: Antifoam A Concentrate (A5633 and A6582)
L83@P1: Antifoam A Concentrate is an extremely effective foam
L84@P1: suppressor for aqueous and non-aqueous systems. It is
L85@P1: 100% active silicone polymer. No emulsifiers are
L86@P1: present. Antifoam A Concentrate is typically effective at
L87@P1: 1-100 ppm. Antifoam A Concentrate should be diluted
L88@P1: with 3-10 parts of propylene glycol (aqueous) or
L89@P1: vegetable oil (nonaqueous) with slow mixing. The
L90@P1: product will be stable in the pH range of 5 to 9.
L91@P1: Antifoam A Concentrate can be added directly to a
L92@P1: fermentation medium, but it is not recommended that it
L93@P1: be pumped to a fermentor on an as-needed basis.
L94@P1: Appearance: Gray liquid
L95@P1: Density: 0.97 g/ml at 25 °C
L96@P1: Antifoam B Emulsion (A5757 and A6707)
L97@P1: Antifoam B Emulsion is an aqueous emulsion
L98@P1: containing 10% active silicone. It contains non-ionic
L99@P1: emulsifiers different from those in Antifoam Emulsions
L100@P1: C and Y-30.
L101@P1: Antifoam B Emulsion can be prediluted with 3-10 parts
L102@P1: of cool water to aid in dispersion. Prediluted
L103@P1: suspensions should be used immediately. Antifoam B
L104@P1: Emulsion is typically effective at 1-100 ppm. The flow
L105@P1: properties of Antifoam B Emulsion are such that it can
L106@P1: be pumped on an as-needed basis to a fermentor
L107@P1: system with sufficient agitation to disperse the antifoam.
L108@P1: Appearance: White emulsion
L109@P1: pH: ~6.5
L110@P1: Density: 1.0 at 25 °C
L111@P1: A8011 Antifoam C Emulsion
L112@P1: Antifoam C Emulsion is an aqueous emulsion
L113@P1: containing 30% active silicone. It contains non-ionic
L114@P1: emulsifiers different from those in Antifoam Emulsions
L115@P1: B and Y-30.
L116@P1: Antifoam C Emulsion can be prediluted with 3-10 parts
L117@P1: of cool water to aid in dispersion. Prediluted
L118@P1: suspensions should be used immediately.
L119@P1: Antifoam C Emulsion is typically effective at 1-10 ppm.
L120@P1: The flow properties of Antifoam C Emulsion are such
L121@P1: that it can be pumped on an as-needed basis to a
L122@P1: fermentor system with sufficient agitation to disperse
L123@P1: the antifoam.
L124@P1: Appearance: White emulsion
L125@P1: pH: ~3
L126@P1: Density: 1.0 at 25 °C
L127@P1: Antifoam Y-30 Emulsion (A5758 and A6457)
L128@P1: Antifoam Y-30 Emulsion is an aqueous emulsion
L129@P1: containing 30% active silicon. It contains non-ionic
L130@P1: emulsifiers different from those in Antifoam Emulsions
L131@P1: B and C.
L132@P1: Antifoam Y-30 Emulsion can be prediluted with
L133@P1: 3-10 parts of cool water to aid in dispersion. Prediluted
L134@P1: suspensions should be used immediately. Antifoam
L135@P1: Y-30 Emulsion is typically effective at 1-100 ppm. The
L136@P1: flow properties of Antifoam Y-30 Emulsion are such that
L137@P1: it can be pumped on an as-needed basis to a fermentor
L138@P1: system with sufficient agitation to disperse the antifoam.
L139@P1: Appearance: White emulsion
L140@P1: pH: ~3
L141@P1: Density: 1.0 at 25 °C
L142@P1: Antifoam SE-15 (A8582)
L143@P1: Antifoam SE-15 is a 10% emulsion of active silicone
L144@P1: polymer and non-ionic emulsifiers. This antifoam is
L145@P1: water-dilutable and effective in both hot and cold
L146@P1: systems. It can be repeatedly sterilized by autoclaving.
L147@P1: The flow properties of Antifoam SE-15 are such that it
L148@P1: can be pumped to a fermentor on an as-needed basis.
L149@P1: Appearance: Milky-white liquid
L150@P1: Density: 1.0 g/ml
L151@P1: Viscosity: 2000 cps
L152@P1: Precautions and Disclaimer
L153@P1: This product is for R&D use only, not for drug,
L154@P1: household, or other uses. Please consult the Material
L155@P1: Safety Data Sheet for information regarding hazards
L156@P1: and safe handling practices.
L157@P1: Storage/Stability
L158@P1: The recommended storage temperature for antifoams is
L159@P1-2: room temperature.Procedure
L160@P2: Antifoams should be added prior to the point where
L161@P2: foaming occurs. Alternatively, antifoam can be used as
L162@P2: supplied, by wiping on filling nozzles, rims of processing
L163@P2: vats, or on a screen suspended above the foaming
L164@P2: system. One of the most common applications for
L165@P2: antifoams is in microbiological fermentation.
L166@P2: Since one cannot predict the effectiveness of an
L167@P2: antifoam for a particular application, antifoams should
L168@P2: also be tested to ensure adequate defoaming
L169@P2: effectiveness under representative culture conditions
L170@P2: for each microorganism. The variables of medium
L171@P2: composition, temperature, pH, mixing, and aeration
L172@P2: anticipated for the final experimental or fermentation
L173@P2: conditions should be used. If the antifoam is not
L174@P2: effective under these test conditions either a higher
L175@P2: amount of antifoam can be added or a different type of
L176@P2: antifoam can be tested.
L177@P2: Applications
L178@P2: The application of antifoam silicones in the
L179@P2: microbiological fermentation technique.1
L180@P2: Foam formation and the subsequent cell damage/
L181@P2: losses in the foam layer were found to be the major
L182@P2: problems affecting cell growth and monoclonal antibody
L183@P2: (MAb) production in stirred and sparged bioreactors for
L184@P2: both serum-supplemented and serum-free media.
L185@P2: Surfactants in the culture media had a profound effect
L186@P2: on cell growth by changing both the properties of
L187@P2: bubbles and the qualities of foam formed.2 Addition of
L188@P2: high concentrations of silicone antifoam to a
L189@P2: suspension of hybridoma cells in a bubble column
L190@P2: reduces the death rate when using medium without a
L191@P2: protective component.3
L192@P2: The mechanism of antifoaming in a nonionic Triton
L193@P2: X-100 surfactant solution with silicone polyethers, the
L194@P2: so-called "cloud point antifoams," was investigated. The
L195@P2: cloud point (CP) studies showed that the CP of a Triton
L196@P2: X-100/silicone polyether mixed system is between the
L197@P2: CP of the foaming and the antifoam surfactants, due to
L198@P2: mixed micelle formation.4
L199@P2: Supercritical carbon dioxide was used for the direct
L200@P2: extraction of drugs from plasma prior to analysis. The
L201@P2: supercritical fluid was directly passed through plasma
L202@P2: samples spiked with either a neutral (flavone) or an
L203@P2: acidic (ketorolac) drug. The addition of an antifoam
L204@P2: agent to the plasma prior to extraction was required to
L205@P2: avoid restrictor plugging caused by denaturation of the
L206@P2: plasma proteins by the supercritical fluid.5
